newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico 48-hour peso reverses firmness on swaps.
newsitem.headline: Mexico 48-hour peso reverses firmness on swaps.

text.p: The 48-hour peso reversed early firmness to close very slightly weaker on Thursday, after a session marked by a high volume of swaps ahead of the long weekend, traders said.

"Liquidity was good...mainly because of foreigners stepping in to invest in the money market, but also in stocks," a trader said. Many traders earlier sold dollars in the same-day market, to buy them back in the 48-hour market, with the advantage they do not have to be paid for until next Tuesday. Mexican fiancial markets will be closed on Monday, September 16, for the Independence Day holiday.

The peso opened firm as U.S. long bond rates eased, but late demand for dollars in the 48-hour market weakened the peso 0.05 of a centavo, compared with Wednesday, to close at 7.5435/7.5470 per dollar. The 24-hour peso closed 1.15 centavos stronger, meanwhile, to 7.5275/7.5325, as there was much less demand for dollars in that market.

"What (local) banks were looking for was to cover themselves in the 48-hour market against any possible risks over the long weekend," a trader said. "Nonetheless, the effect of demand on the 48-hour rate was diminished by ample liquidity in the market."
Traders said the market was cautious with a long weekend ahead due to the precedent of recent guerrilla attacks in Mexico.
